solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Voice opposing general drift (12)

blocks.note: the tenor of an argument is its general drift

annotation.surface: Someone's voice is raised against the prevailing mood of a discussion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Voice' looks like a verb (to voice an objection), but it is the noun: a kind of singing voice.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the countertenor is the highest adult male singing voice, above the tenor.

entries.clue: Punctuation mark that’s part of tract (5)

blocks.note: the mark made of two dots stacked one above the other
the large intestine, part of the digestive tract

annotation.surface: A grammar note about a mark appearing in a pamphlet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tract' suggests a religious pamphlet full of punctuation; here it is the intestinal tract.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses share one spelling: the punctuation mark and the main section of the large intestine.

entries.clue: Lacking flexibility, not stopping to take in Britain (9)

indicatorNotes.to take in: to take something in is to admit it inside, so the outer word opens up and holds the letter

blocks.note: unending = not stopping, going on for ever
B is the standard abbreviation for Britain, as on car stickers

annotation.surface: A rigid, restless tourist who won't pause to see Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: The inserted letter goes in after the first two letters, splitting the negative prefix from the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unbending is rigid, whether of a bar or of a stubborn attitude.

entries.clue: Last train can’t break down crossing pond (13)

indicatorNotes.break down: a thing that breaks down falls to pieces, so the letters come apart to be rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: A commuter worries the final train of the night will fail on its way over the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The pond' is jocular slang for the Atlantic Ocean, which is why a train cannot really be crossing it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'the pond' is a humorous name for the Atlantic, so crossing it is transatlantic.

entries.clue: I creep around to get set of instructions (6)

indicatorNotes.around: moving around means shifting position, so the letters change places

annotation.surface: Someone sneaks about to find the instructions for something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' reads as an adverb of creeping; it is really telling you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The everyday cooking sense: the method for a dish is written as a list of steps to follow.

entries.clue: Former name given to one country’s destruction (13)

blocks.note: a term is a name for something
a nation is a country; the 's joins it to the definition

annotation.surface: A country's former name is linked to its ruin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former name' reads as a single idea, a country's old name, but the two words give separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though stronger: to exterminate is to wipe out entirely.

entries.clue: Row, expelling hot air at regular intervals (3)

indicatorNotes.expelling: to expel is to throw out, so some letters of the fodder are discarded
indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: evenly spaced, so every other letter is thrown out

annotation.surface: An argument where the parties periodically vent a lot of empty talk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, which suits 'hot air', but it is rowing a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to oar is an old word for to row, propelling a boat with oars.

entries.clue: Maiden over fixed (6)

blocks.note: M = maiden (over) on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A cricket accusation: a maiden over was rigged.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden over is six balls with no runs scored; the clue splits the phrase so 'over' means finished. 'Fixed' suggests match-fixing but means repaired.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the repair sense of 'fixed', not the rigged sense the cricket surface suggests.

entries.clue: Mediterranean country turning in waybill (5)

indicatorNotes.turning: something turning faces the other way, so the letters are read right to left
indicatorNotes.in: the answer is contained in the next word

blocks.note: the 2nd to 6th letters of the word, read right to left

annotation.surface: A shipping document for a Mediterranean destination.
annotation.walkthrough: A waybill is a document listing goods being shipped, so the surface is about freight.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Libya lies on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

entries.clue: Social circle in crib by lake (7)

blocks.note: a cot is a baby's crib
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes; 'by' puts it next to the crib

annotation.surface: A group of friends gathered in a cabin by the lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it only links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word, from French, means a small exclusive clique.

entries.clue: Either way round, she’s in order (3)

indicatorNotes.Either way round: whichever way round you read it, the word is the same

blocks.note: palindrome indicator: the answer must read the same forwards and backwards

annotation.surface: Someone is being reassured that all is tidy, whichever way you look at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In order' sounds like tidy; it means a member of a religious order.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style definition: a woman who has joined a religious order is literally 'in order'.

entries.clue: Returned copies evaluated and split up (9)

indicatorNotes.Returned: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

annotation.surface: Graded papers handed back to students, then divided among them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copies' is the verb: to ape someone is to copy them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: split up and separated both mean parted, as a couple or a set of items might be.

entries.clue: Picks up date in Rome to join party? (4,5)

blocks.note: a fixed day in the ancient Roman calendar, the 13th or 15th of the month

annotation.surface: Someone collects a companion in Rome to go to a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a faction, not a celebration; the question mark flags that the definition is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take sides is to align with one party in a dispute, loosely 'joining' it.

entries.clue: Authority in charge of football international lacking conviction (5)

blocks.note: the Football Association, English football's governing body
INT is the abbreviation for international

annotation.surface: An international football body is criticised for being half-hearted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'International' looks like part of the football phrase, but it is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: The half-hearted sense, as in faint praise or a faint attempt, rather than swooning.

entries.clue: Meat wrapped in iron — a match needed for this dish? (6)

annotation.definition: a match needed for this dish?
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase describing the dish, which is set alight

indicatorNotes.wrapped in: something wrapped in a covering is enclosed by it, so the meat sits inside the iron

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: A cook wraps meat in foil and asks whether it needs to be lit.
annotation.walkthrough: A flambé is a dish doused in spirits and set alight, hence the match.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a flambéed dish is set on fire at the table, so it needs a match.

entries.clue: Half-hearted kidder’s upset and annoyed (5)

indicatorNotes.Half-hearted: the heart is the middle of the word, and half of it goes
indicatorNotes.upset: to upset is to knock over, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: KIDDER with one of its two middle Ds dropped

annotation.surface: A joker whose heart isn't in it is upset and irritable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' is literal: the heart of the word is a double letter, and only one survives.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to irk is to irritate, so irked means annoyed.

entries.clue: I very much exclude feature of weather map (6)

blocks.note: so = very much, as in 'so tired'

annotation.surface: Someone firmly leaves a detail off a weather chart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very much' reads as an intensifier on 'exclude', but it is a piece of its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: isobars are the lines joining points of equal pressure on a weather map.

entries.clue: Wasted an age with ease in waters off Greece (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Wasted: wasted means ruined, or slang for drunk, and either way the letters fall into disorder

annotation.surface: A long, lazy holiday idled away on the Greek sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' just joins the two lots of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey.

entries.clue: Post Office making U-turn after small concession (3)

indicatorNotes.making U-turn: a vehicle making a U-turn heads back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.after: coming after means following, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A post office reverses a decision after a minor compromise.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in the order the clue gives it, but the answer puts the small piece first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sop is a small concession offered to placate someone.

entries.clue: Half of nationalist party in tartan (5)

indicatorNotes.Half of: the party's name has two words, and half of it is one of them

blocks.note: the Welsh nationalist party; keep the first word of its two-word name and drop CYMRU

annotation.surface: A political party's members dressed in tartan.
annotation.walkthrough: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party; 'half' is one word of its two-word name, not half the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: plaid is tartan cloth or its checked pattern, the American word for it.

entries.clue: Place for soak that’s squiffy, into bubbly? Not half (7)

indicatorNotes.squiffy: squiffy means tipsy, so the letters stagger into a new order
indicatorNotes.into: going into something means ending up inside it
indicatorNotes.Not half: not half means only half is used

annotation.surface: A tipsy drinker of champagne heads for a long soak.
annotation.walkthrough: Squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk, and bubbly is champagne.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a soak is a long bath, and the tub is where you take it.

entries.clue: Attempt touchdown (3)

blocks.note: in rugby, grounding the ball over the opponents' line scores five points

annotation.surface: A sports commentator calls an attempt to score.
annotation.walkthrough: In rugby the score for grounding the ball behind the opponents' line is named for the attempt it once earned at a kick.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an attempt at anything, and the rugby score made by touching the ball down.

entries.clue: Train diagram covering the country (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: the two words cover the answer, holding it between their outer letters

blocks.note: the last two letters of the first word and the first three of the second

annotation.surface: A railway map showing lines across a whole nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the famous railways of the answer, which helps hide it across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one country, and 'the' points to a single one.

entries.clue: Scorned shiny fragments pulled together (12)

indicatorNotes.fragments: as a verb, to fragment is to break into pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: Rejected glittering shards are gathered up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fragments' looks like a noun but works as a verb: the fodder fragments.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: things synchronised act in unison, as a team does when it pulls together.
